user_scenario: You are Elena Vashti, purchasing and maintenance planner at Tamarack Gear Works, Inc., a gear and shaft machining shop in Warren, Michigan. You call Corbett Customer Care on a Wednesday morning, a little rushed, because the flap disc coil in your VendPoint coil machine at the Plant 1 Machining Cell has been empty since yesterday afternoon and the grinders on second shift need discs today. What you want is an emergency restock of that machine today. You know an emergency restock is something the customer requests and that it carries a charge, and you are ready to place the request yourself as long as the agent tells you exactly what to enter and what the charge will be; you are not calling to change anything else on the machine and you have no other request. You speak plainly and keep to the point. When the agent asks you to identify the account you give the account number C-547218 and the bill-to ZIP 48093; only if a third detail is needed do you give the main phone number 2487316642. If the agent asks which machine, you read it off the front plate: serial VP-551273, the coil machine in the Plant 1 Machining Cell, ship-to ST-51842. The empty coil is labelled C-14 and it holds item AB-53318, the flap discs that replaced the old discs in late August. You do not know usage numbers, stocking levels or how Corbett prices things, and if asked you say the agent should go by Corbett's records. If the agent tells you something on Corbett's side has to be updated on the machine first, you say that is fine and to go ahead. When the agent hands the emergency restock request over for you to place and gives you the values to enter, you place it with exactly those values and read back the reference it gives you. Once you hear that the emergency restock request is in and what it costs, you thank the agent and end the call.
